newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU declines comment on C.Lyonnais early sell off.
newsitem.headline: EU declines comment on C.Lyonnais early sell off.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner declined to comment on Thursday on the French government pldge to sell embattled Credit Lyonnais earlier than originally expected.

But he sounded doubtful that this would happen. "Did he say so," Van Miert said with an amused look when asked to react to Finance Minister Jean Arthuis announcement on Wednesday that the bank would be sold as soon as possible following a third rescue plan for the ailing bank.
"There is no comment for the moment," Van Miert told Reuters after speaking at a meeting of the European Parliament's monetary and economic affairs committee.

Earlier at the meeting he reacted to criticism from British Socialist Alan Donnelly that the Commission was bowing to French pressure by allowing emergency aid of 3.9 billion French francs on Wednesday.
"Credit Lyonnais will go down in history as a case where the Commission has bent its knee in the face of pressure from the French government," Donnelly said.
Van Miert defended the Commission's decision, which he said had been unanimous:
"The facts are on our side: we have been tough...we did not bend the rules because of pressure."
Van Miert also warned against jumping to the conclusion that the Commission would simply clear the bank's third rescue package in three years.
"No one can prejudge the outcome of the investigation of the case."
But at the same time he stressed the specificity of the case -- a huge company in a sector where failure of one of the main players could have devastating effects for the whole industry.

Credit Lyonnais was the first case of state aid in the banking sector the Commission had to deal with in 1995. Advised by a group of former European central bank governors it concluded at the time the sector was "sensitive" and "specific" although it also said this did not mean it was immune from EU competition rules. -- Amelia Torres 322 2876841
